blocks.text: SITHEMR is a unified electronic medical records platform built for Philippine hospitals. It streamlines patient care, PhilHealth compliance, and clinical workflows across a single integrated system supporting OPD, ER, in-patient admission, obstetrics, delivery, operating room, nursing, laboratory, radiology, pharmacy, procedures, CSR/supply chain, billing, renal care, ICU/MICU, YAKAP (community health), and Konsulta services.

Access SITHEMR through a modern web browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari). No additional client software is needed. The application runs on the hospital server and is accessed over the local network or secure internet connection.
Navigate to the login page at:
Enter your email address and password. Click "Sign In to Dashboard". If you forget your password, contact your hospital administrator.

items: Email: admin@demohospital.com
Password: Admin@12345

runs.text: Change the default password immediately after first login. Never share your credentials with others.

blocks.text: SITHEMR uses role-based access control (RBAC). Your permissions are determined by your assigned role:

items: Super Admin — Full system access across all hospitals. Manages users, roles, permissions, and system settings.
Tenant Admin — Hospital-level administrator. Manages departments, users, and settings for their hospital.
Doctor — Access to patient charts, appointment scheduling, and clinical documentation.
Staff — Clinical and administrative staff with permissions tailored to their functions (nursing, lab, pharmacy, billing, etc.).

blocks.text: If you attempt to access a page without the required permission, you will be redirected with an error message. Contact your administrator to request additional permissions.
After logging in, you are directed to the Dashboard (Command Center). This is your central hub showing:

items: Live Patient Census — current inpatient count across wards
Financial Snapshot — billed today, collected today, total outstanding
PhilHealth E-Claims Tracker — monthly performance and submission status
Quick navigation to all modules via the left sidebar

Click the Patients menu to open the patient registration page.
Fill in personal information: last name, first name, middle name, birthday, gender, civil status, nationality, religion, occupation, blood type, and contact details.
Enter the patient's address: baranggay, city/municipality, province, and region.
Add PhilHealth information if available: PhilHealth member ID and coverage details.
Click Save to create the patient record. The system generates a unique patient ID.
Verify the information is correct before saving. Some fields may be required depending on configuration.

runs.text: Use the search bar to find existing patients before creating a new record to avoid duplicates.

blocks.text: Search for patients by name, patient ID, or PhilHealth member ID. The patient list shows key information at a glance. Click a patient to view their full record including demographics, contacts, and visit history.

items: Navigate to OPD > Consultations.
Select the patient from the search or patient list.
Choose the consultation type (e.g., new visit, follow-up, referral).
Select the clinic and attending physician.
Enter the chief complaint and clinical findings.
Add assessment and diagnosis using ICD10 codes.
Create prescriptions, laboratory orders, or other referrals as needed.
Save the consultation record.

blocks.text: Consultations are timestamped and linked to the patient's medical record for continuity of care.
Configure the following OPD master data items as needed:

items: Visit Types — e.g., New Patient, Follow-up, Referral
Consultation Types — e.g., General Consultation, Specialty Consultation
Referral Sources — where the patient came from
Services — OPD services and procedures
Clinics — OPD clinics and their specialties
Complaints — common chief complaints for quick entry

runs.text: Emergency Room menu (permission: er.triage or er.manage)

items: Navigate to ER > Triage.
Register the patient or select an existing patient.
Assess and record vital signs.
Assign an acuity level (e.g., Emergency, Urgent, Non-urgent) based on the patient's condition.
Record the chief complaint and initial observations.
Assign the patient to an ER bed and zone.
The triage record feeds into the ER admission for further management.
Navigate to ER > Beds or Admissions.
Select a triage record or create a new admission.
Assign an attending physician.
Record the diagnosis and treatment plan.
Create OECB (Office of Extension and Coordinated Billing) entries for PhilHealth billing.
Track the patient's status: admitted, treated, transferred, or discharged.
Generate the EECL PDF for PhilHealth claims when the patient is discharged.

blocks.text: ER beds and zones are configurable under ER > Beds and ER > Zones. Acuity levels and mobility statuses are managed under ER > Acuity Levels and ER > Mobility Statuses.

items: Navigate to Admission & Wards > Admissions.
Search for the patient or create a new patient record.
Assign the patient to a ward, room, and bed.
Select the attending physician and admission type.
Record the admitting diagnosis and clinical notes.
Track the admission status: admitted, transferred, discharged, or admitted to ICU.
Manage room transfers via Admission & Wards > Room History.

blocks.text: The Orders tab allows batch ordering across multiple departments. Orders are placed in a queue and can be submitted together. A batch queue system with auto-save on tab switch preserves selections when navigating between order types (Lab, Pharmacy, CSR, Radiology, Procedures).

Navigate to Lab > Results or Lab > Dispensing.
Create a new lab request for a patient.
Add lab tests to the request (individual tests or panels).
Assign the requesting doctor and specimen collection details.
Track request status: Pending, Collected, Processing, Completed, or Cancelled.
Enter test results with reference range comparisons.
Verify and validate results (separate roles for performer, verifier, and validator).
Print results using Lab > Results > Print.
Modalities — Imaging equipment (e.g., X-Ray, CT Scan, MRI, Ultrasound)

Navigate to Radiology > Results or Radiology > Dispensing.
Create a radiology request with the exam type and body part.
Assign the requesting doctor and radiologist.
Track request status through the workflow.
Upload and link DICOM images from PACS for the exam.
Enter preliminary and final findings.
Sign off on the final report.
Print results with images using Radiology > Results > Print.

blocks.text: DICOM/PACS integration allows querying studies, retrieving images, generating thumbnails, and storing images. The DICOM API includes study queries, worklist access, and image storage endpoints.

Navigate to Pharmacy > Dispensing.
Select the patient and the prescribing doctor.
Choose the drugs to dispense from inventory.
Select the drug batch (for expiry tracking).
Specify dosage, quantity, and directions.
Process the dispensing record.
Print the pharmacy request receipt if required.

blocks.text: The Patient Medication Record provides a complete history of all medications dispensed to a patient across visits.

blocks.text: To print a statement of account: navigate to Billing > Statement, select the patient, choose Summary or Detailed mode, and generate the PDF. The statement shows all charges, payments, and the running balance.

Navigate to PhilHealth > Claims.
Create a new claim linked to an ER admission, OPD consultation, or in-patient admission.
Link the patient's PhilHealth membership.
Select the ICD10 diagnosis codes (primary, secondary, tertiary).
Assign the case rate and attending/referring physicians.
Add claim items (consultations, procedures, medicines, diagnostics).
Link the claim to a claim batch for bulk submission.
Generate claim PDFs: CF1, CF2, CF3, CF4, CF5, ESOA, and EECL forms.
Submit the claim batch via the eClaims service.

blocks.text: PhilHealth eClaims Integration: The system connects to the PhilHealth eClaims portal for electronic claim submission. Claims are formatted according to PhilHealth standards (CF1-CF5, ESOA, EECL) and submitted in XML format. The system supports shadow billing (CF5) for OECB-covered patients and status polling to track claim acceptance or rejection.

items: CF1 — In-patient claims (medical/surgical)
CF2 — In-patient claims with referring physician
CF3 — Delivery claims
CF4 — In-patient claims with secondary diagnosis
CF5 — Out-patient/shadow billing claims
ESOA — Electronic Summary of Official Assessment
EECL — Emergency Case Labor and Delivery

runs.text: Doctors Portal (permission: doctors.dashboard), Patient Scheduling (permission: doctors.schedule) or public booking at /book-appointment

items: Today's schedule and appointments
Patient list for the day
Pending consultations and results to review
Quick access to patient charts

blocks.text: Access patient charts via Doctors > Patient > [type] > [id]. The chart shows the patient's complete clinical history including demographics, visit history (OPD, ER, admission), diagnoses and ICD10 codes, medications and prescriptions, laboratory and radiology results, and clinical notes.
Patients can book appointments without logging in:

items: Go to /book-appointment (or click Book an Appointment on the login page).
Select a department (e.g., Cardiology, General Surgery, Pediatrics).
Choose a doctor from the selected department.
Pick an appointment date (must be today or later).
Select an available time slot from the grid. Slots are 30-minute intervals between 8:00 AM and 5:00 PM. Already-booked slots are shown as unavailable.
Enter patient name (required), phone, email, and reason for visit.
Submit the booking. A confirmation code (e.g., APT-00001) is issued.

blocks.text: Slots are generated automatically based on the doctor's schedule. The system prevents double-booking by checking for conflicts at the time of booking. Working hours and slot duration are configured in the appointment settings.

items: Navigate to Doctors > Schedule (or Patient Scheduling in the sidebar).
View all appointments with filters for status, date, and doctor.
Search appointments by patient name, reference code, or doctor.
Click an appointment to open the edit/reschedule modal.
Reschedule: change the date and pick a new available slot.
Update status: Scheduled, In Progress, Completed, or Cancelled.
Add or edit notes for the appointment.
Non-admin doctors see only their own appointments.

blocks.text: Manage obstetric consultations: select the pregnant patient, record gestational age and fetal presentation, document the assessment and plan, add ordered tests or referrals, and save. OB master data includes visit types, fetal presentations, and contraceptive methods for post-partum counseling.

blocks.text: To process a CSR request: navigate to CSR / Supply > Dispensing, create a request for a patient or department, add supply items with quantities, assign the requesting department, process the request (approve and dispense), and print the CSR request receipt or encounter print.

items: Dialysis Types — Types of dialysis (e.g., Hemodialysis, Peritoneal Dialysis)

Navigate to Medical Records.
Select the certificate type (e.g., Medical Certificate, Fit to Work, Sick Certificate).
Choose the encounter type (OPD, ER Treatment, or Admission) and enter the encounter ID and patient ID.
The system pulls patient and encounter data automatically.
Review and print the certificate.

runs.text: Masters menu (permission: admin.masters, admin.departments, admin.users, or admin.tenants)

blocks.text: Super Admins manage hospitals (tenants): create and edit hospital records (name, address, contact, PhilHealth accreditation), activate or deactivate hospitals. Each hospital is a separate tenant with its own users, patients, and data.

items: Create departments (e.g., Cardiology, General Surgery, Pediatrics, Orthopedics)
Assign departments to hospitals (tenants)
Set department active status
Navigate to Masters > Users.
Create a new user with username, full name, email, password, and role.
Assign the user to a hospital (tenant).
Set the user's active status.
Optionally link the user to a health care professional record.
Manage individual user permissions via Masters > Users > [user] > Permissions.
Record professional details: name, type (physician, nurse, etc.), specialization, license number
Link professionals to departments
Health care professionals are referenced in consultations, admissions, and orders

blocks.text: Manage patient transfers between hospitals or facilities. Track transfer requests, approvals, and patient movement records. Admission room history tracks patient room transfers within the hospital (ward changes, bed moves, ICU transfers) with timestamps and reasons.

rows: Verify email and password. Contact admin if account is disabled.
Contact your administrator to request the required permission.
Patient may not be registered or search term is incorrect
Try searching by patient ID or PhilHealth member ID. Register a new patient if needed.
Slot is already booked or outside working hours
Choose a different time slot or date. Slots outside 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM are not available.
Result not yet verified or validated
Contact the lab or radiology technician. Results require verification before they appear in the patient chart.
Network issue or incorrect claim data
Verify the claim data is complete. Check network connectivity to the PhilHealth eClaims portal. Retry the submission.
Ensure all required fields are filled. Check server logs for detailed error messages.
